clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying the orchard, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote daily to her sister; Walter spent long days out in the trees and grew distant from June; Glen got into fights at school; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that winter; Walter and June rowed over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, marking where the family settled into the new place.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan, within the following year: Walter drank heavily most nights; Walter and Glen blamed each other for the loan and rowed; after the auction in October, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969; Ida's heart trouble was found and she stopped working at the bakery. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning trees, marking where the family's acute crisis eased.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the following year: Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard for hours; Glen and Marian fought loudly over money at night; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora kept to her room and grew distant from her mother; Walter drank again after six years off it. By June 1976, when Glen started driving a delivery truck for the feed store, Nora was eating again and made the track team, marking where the family settled.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving from her farm into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990, within the following year: Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis rowed most nights. By June 1991, when Wilma took a flat in town, Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, marking where the household settled.
